idiom: hit the nail on the head
meaning: to describe or identify exactly the right thing or the real cause of a problem
literal_translation: tam üstüne basmak (tam isabet etmek, sorunu tam olarak doğru tespit etmek)
example: Your comment hit the nail on the head: the budget was the real problem all along.
origin: Comes from carpentry, where a hammer strikes the head of a nail squarely, driving it in with one precise blow

wrong_meanings.meaning: to use a hammer carelessly on a wall
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This describes a literal action of construction, but the idiom is not about carpentry or physical work

wrong_meanings.meaning: to make a loud noise during a meeting
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom has nothing to do with noise or disruption; it describes accuracy in understanding or speaking

wrong_meanings.meaning: to miss the main point of a discussion
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the opposite of the idiom, which means identifying the main point exactly

explanation: 'Hit the nail on the head' comes from carpentry and means saying or identifying exactly what is correct or essential in a situation.
